@graph.headline: How to Measure PR ROI and Share of Voice in 2026
@graph.alternativeHeadline: The four metrics that map crypto PR to pipeline, plus a board-ready reporting framework
@graph.description: Impressions, AVE, and clip counts are not PR ROI metrics. This 2026 framework covers the four measures that actually map PR to pipeline: share of voice against a named competitive set, tier-weighted placement volume, branded search lift, and inbound attribution. Includes a board reporting template, SOV calculation method, and the emerging AI citation share metric.

itemListElement.name: How to Measure PR ROI and Share of Voice in 2026

mainEntity.name: How do you measure PR ROI for a crypto or Web3 project?

acceptedAnswer.text: The four metrics that actually map PR to outcomes are: share of voice against a named competitive set, tier-weighted placement volume (not raw clip count), branded search lift tracked in Google Search Console, and inbound attribution (investors and partners who name a specific piece as their first touchpoint). Impressions, AVE, and total clip counts are not useful ROI proxies. A CoinDesk feature and a wire republish should never count the same.

mainEntity.name: What is share of voice and how do you calculate it for crypto PR?

acceptedAnswer.text: Share of voice is your percentage of total media mentions in a defined competitive set. You pick four to six direct competitors, pull monthly mention volume from a monitoring tool, and divide your mentions by the total across the entire set. If total mentions across six protocols in a month are 2,000 and 340 name you, your SOV is 17 percent. You track the ratio over time, not the raw number.

mainEntity.name: What should a crypto PR board report include?

acceptedAnswer.text: One slide, four data points: the SOV trend line for the last three to six months, the tier-1 and tier-2 placement count for the period (with a note on the most significant piece and what it drove), a branded search lift chart from Google Search Console, and cost per credible placement. Leave out impressions, AVE, and total reach. Boards care whether PR is moving pipeline and investor awareness, not whether you hit a clip count target.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take for PR coverage to show up in search or inbound metrics?

acceptedAnswer.text: The lag is typically six to twelve weeks between a sustained PR push and measurable branded search lift. Inbound attribution is faster, often two to four weeks after a major tier-1 placement, because investors and partners read the outlet in real time. Search compounding takes longer because it depends on indexing, link equity accumulation, and AI engine re-crawl cycles. Track both on separate timelines and do not expect instant correlation.

mainEntity.name: Is there a way to measure whether PR is helping with AI search citations?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, though no single tool does it cleanly yet. The practical method is a weekly sample: pick ten to fifteen questions your target buyer or investor would ask in your category, run them in ChatGPT and Perplexity, and log whether your brand appears in the answer or citations. Over a quarter the trend becomes clear. Tier-1 editorial coverage and bylined founder content are the primary drivers of AI citation share, so it compounds directly from strong PR.
